#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Boots the API on a scratch SQLite database, runs the vendored official
# RealWorld Hurl suite against it, then tears the server down.
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
cd "$ROOT"

PORT="${PORT:-8000}"
HOST="${HOST:-http://localhost:$PORT}"
UID_VAL="${UID_VAL:-$(date +%s)$$}"
SERVER_LOG="$ROOT/.hurl-server.log"

if ! command -v hurl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "error: hurl is not installed (see https://hurl.dev)" >&2
  exit 127
fi

export DATABASE_URL="${DATABASE_URL:-file:./test.db}"
export PORT
export LOG=off

npm run --silent db:setup >/dev/null

npx tsx src/index.ts >"$SERVER_LOG" 2>&1 &
SERVER_PID=$!

cleanup() {
  kill "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
  wait "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
}
trap cleanup EXIT

echo "Waiting for $HOST ..."
for _ in $(seq 1 60); do
  if curl -fsS "$HOST/health" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    break
  fi
  if ! kill -0 "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "error: server exited during startup" >&2
    cat "$SERVER_LOG" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  sleep 0.5
done

echo "Running Hurl tests against $HOST with uid=$UID_VAL"

FILES=("$@")
if [ ${#FILES[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
  FILES=("$ROOT"/tests/hurl/*.hurl)
fi

hurl --test \
  --jobs 1 \
  --variable "host=$HOST" \
  --variable "uid=$UID_VAL" \
  "${FILES[@]}"

# RealWorld Hurl suite against it, then tears the server down.
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
cd "$ROOT"

PORT="${PORT:-8000}"
HOST="${HOST:-http://localhost:$PORT}"
UID_VAL="${UID_VAL:-$(date +%s)$$}"
SERVER_LOG="$ROOT/.hurl-server.log"

# An unrelated npm package also ships a `hurl` binary, so pick the first entry on
# PATH that actually reports itself as Hurl (https://hurl.dev).
resolve_hurl() {
  if [ -n "${HURL_BIN:-}" ]; then
    echo "$HURL_BIN"
    return 0
  fi
  local candidate
  while IFS= read -r candidate; do
    if "$candidate" --version 2>/dev/null | head -n 1 | grep -qE '^hurl [0-9]'; then
      echo "$candidate"
      return 0
    fi
  done < <(type -a -p hurl 2>/dev/null)
  return 1
}

HURL="$(resolve_hurl)" || {
  echo "error: hurl is not installed (see https://hurl.dev)" >&2
  exit 127
}
echo "Using hurl at $HURL ($("$HURL" --version | head -n 1))"

export DATABASE_URL="${DATABASE_URL:-file:./test.db}"
export PORT
export LOG=off

npm run --silent db:setup >/dev/null

npx tsx src/index.ts >"$SERVER_LOG" 2>&1 &
SERVER_PID=$!

cleanup() {
  kill "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
  wait "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
}
trap cleanup EXIT

echo "Waiting for $HOST ..."
for _ in $(seq 1 60); do
  if curl -fsS "$HOST/health" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    break
  fi
  if ! kill -0 "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "error: server exited during startup" >&2
    cat "$SERVER_LOG" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  sleep 0.5
done

echo "Running Hurl tests against $HOST with uid=$UID_VAL"

FILES=("$@")
if [ ${#FILES[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
  FILES=("$ROOT"/tests/hurl/*.hurl)
fi

hurl --test \
  --jobs 1 \
  --variable "host=$HOST" \
  --variable "uid=$UID_VAL" \
  "${FILES[@]}"

# RealWorld Backend — TypeScript + Fastify + Prisma + SQLite

A complete implementation of the [RealWorld backend specification](https://realworld-docs.netlify.app/specifications/backend/endpoints/):
JWT authentication, users and profiles, article CRUD, comments, favorites, tags and the personalized feed.

The official RealWorld Hurl suite is vendored into `tests/hurl/` and passes in full — **13 files, 154 requests**.

## Requirements

- Node.js 20 or newer
- [Hurl](https://hurl.dev) (only needed to run the API test suite)

## Getting started

```bash
npm install
npm run dev
```

`npm run dev` generates the Prisma client, syncs the SQLite schema and starts the
server with hot reload on <http://localhost:8000>. No other setup step is required.

| Script            | What it does                                                       |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `npm run dev`     | Set up the database, then run the server with watch mode            |
| `npm start`       | Set up the database, then run the server once                       |
| `npm run db:setup`| `prisma generate` + `prisma db push`                                |
| `npm run build`   | Type-check the project (`tsc --noEmit`)                             |
| `npm run test:api`| Boot the server on a scratch database and run the Hurl suite        |

Configuration comes from `.env`:

| Variable       | Default                             | Purpose                        |
| -------------- | ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| `DATABASE_URL` | `file:./dev.db`                     | SQLite database location       |
| `JWT_SECRET`   | `realworld-dev-secret-change-me`    | Token signing secret           |
| `PORT`         | `8000`                              | HTTP port                      |

## Running the API tests

```bash
npm run test:api
```

The runner starts the API against `file:./test.db`, waits for `/health`, runs every
file in `tests/hurl/`, and shuts the server down afterwards. Pass specific files to
narrow the run:

```bash
npm run test:api -- tests/hurl/articles.hurl
```

If another `hurl` binary shadows the real one on your `PATH`, the script detects it
and picks the correct executable; you can also force one with `HURL_BIN=/path/to/hurl`.

## Endpoints

| Method   | Path                                  | Auth      |
| -------- | ------------------------------------- | --------- |
| `POST`   | `/api/users`                          | –         |
| `POST`   | `/api/users/login`                    | –         |
| `GET`    | `/api/user`                           | required  |
| `PUT`    | `/api/user`                           | required  |
| `GET`    | `/api/profiles/:username`             | optional  |
| `POST`   | `/api/profiles/:username/follow`      | required  |
| `DELETE` | `/api/profiles/:username/follow`      | required  |
| `GET`    | `/api/articles`                       | optional  |
| `GET`    | `/api/articles/feed`                  | required  |
| `POST`   | `/api/articles`                       | required  |
| `GET`    | `/api/articles/:slug`                 | optional  |
| `PUT`    | `/api/articles/:slug`                 | required  |
| `DELETE` | `/api/articles/:slug`                 | required  |
| `POST`   | `/api/articles/:slug/favorite`        | required  |
| `DELETE` | `/api/articles/:slug/favorite`        | required  |
| `GET`    | `/api/articles/:slug/comments`        | optional  |
| `POST`   | `/api/articles/:slug/comments`        | required  |
| `DELETE` | `/api/articles/:slug/comments/:id`    | required  |
| `GET`    | `/api/tags`                           | –         |

`GET /api/articles` accepts `tag`, `author`, `favorited`, `limit` (default 20) and
`offset` (default 0). `articlesCount` always reports the total number of matches,
not the size of the returned page.

Authenticated requests use the RealWorld scheme `Authorization: Token <jwt>`;
`Bearer` is accepted as well.

## Conventions this implementation follows

The vendored test suite pins down a number of behaviours that the prose spec leaves open:

- **Status codes** — `201` for creating users, articles and comments; `204` with an
  empty body for deletions; `409` for a duplicate username or email; `422` for
  validation failures; `403` when acting on someone else's article or comment.
- **Error shape** — always `{"errors": {"<field>": ["<message>"]}}`, e.g.
  `{"errors": {"article": ["not found"]}}` or `{"errors": {"token": ["is missing"]}}`.
- **Nullable profile fields** — `bio` and `image` default to `null`; sending either as
  `""` or `null` in `PUT /api/user` stores `null`.
- **Non-nullable fields** — sending `username`, `email` or `password` as `""` or `null`
  is rejected with `422`.
- **Passwords** — NIST SP 800-63B 5.1.1.2: minimum 8 characters, at least 64 accepted,
  no composition rules.
- **`tagList` on update** — omitting it preserves the current tags, `[]` clears them,
  and `null` is rejected with `422`.
- **Article lists** — the multiple-article payload omits `body` entirely, and articles
  are ordered newest first (ties broken by id, so rapid inserts still paginate stably).
- **Slugs** — derived from the title; duplicate titles are allowed and receive distinct
  slugs.

## Project layout

```
prisma/schema.prisma     Data model (User, Follow, Article, Tag, ArticleTag, Comment, Favorite)
src/index.ts             Server bootstrap and graceful shutdown
src/app.ts               Fastify instance, error handler, route registration
src/auth.ts              JWT signing/verification, password hashing, auth guards
src/validation.ts        Payload parsing and RealWorld validation rules
src/serializers.ts       User/profile/article/comment JSON shapes
src/routes/              users, profiles, articles, comments, tags
scripts/run-api-tests.sh Hurl runner (boots and tears down the server)
tests/hurl/              Vendored official RealWorld Hurl suite
```

## Test suite provenance

`tests/hurl/` is copied verbatim from `specs/api/hurl` in
[realworld-apps/realworld](https://github.com/realworld-apps/realworld), including the
upstream `run-hurl-tests.sh`. Use `scripts/run-api-tests.sh` instead when you want the
server started for you.
